name: top_quark

phase_0.boundary_condition: electroweak symmetry breaking scale (v ≈ 246 GeV) and Standard Model gauge structure SU(3)_c × SU(2)_L × U(1)_Y

⊢.justification: void state before any top quark exists; no color, flavor, or mass excitation present

⊣.justification: closed boundary containing the full production-decay-measurement process; Higgs VEV sets mass scale

≻.justification: forward morphism creating top-antitop pair via gluon fusion or quark annihilation; increases mass-energy

≺.justification: reverse morphism: top quark descends to lighter products (W+b); mass-energy released

⋈.justification: composition of production → top propagation → weak decay → W decay → final state hadrons/leptons

⊙.justification: self-reference: the top quark as a definite particle with fixed mass, spin, charge, color

∈.justification: splits top quark fate into dominant t→W⁺b (≈99.9%) and suppressed channels (t→H⁺b, FCNC, etc.)

∋.justification: rejoins all decay products into invariant mass peak; detector combines leptonic and hadronic channels

⊤.justification: affirmative arm: CKM-favored, near-unity Yukawa coupling, constructive truth of Standard Model prediction

⊥.justification: negative arm: flavor-changing neutral currents, charged Higgs, BSM modes; constructively refuted by data

⊞.justification: paradice: both dominant and suppressed amplitudes coexist until measurement; interference at detector

⊡.justification: permanent, append-only fixation of collision event in trigger and data acquisition system

phase_2.split_input: on-shell top quark (mass 172.76 GeV, width 1.33 GeV)
split_outputs: dominant channel: t → W⁺ + b (branching ratio 0.999)
suppressed channels: t → H⁺b, t → cγ, t → cZ, t → cg (BR < 10⁻³)
phase_2.fuse_result: reconstructed top mass peak at 172.76 GeV with width dominated by detector resolution
phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: pre-collision vacuum: no top quark excitation, parton distributions only
phase_3.true_description: top quark produced on-shell and decayed via t → W⁺b with W subsequently decaying to observed final state
phase_3.false_description: top quark produced but decayed via suppressed channel, or production failed (background event)
phase_3.both_description: quantum superposition of production amplitude and all decay amplitudes before wavefunction collapse at measurement

steps.domain_action: initialize pre-collision vacuum state — no top quark, only incoming partons
establish vacuum self-reference — SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1) gauge invariance
production vertex — gluon fusion gg→tt̄ or quark annihilation qq̄→tt̄ at √ŝ > 2m_t
compose production with top quark propagator — include Breit-Wigner mass distribution
top quark identity — fix mass 172.76 GeV, charge +2/3, color triplet, spin-1/2
open decay branching — top quark fate splits at weak vertex
dominant decay arm — t → W⁺b via V_tb ≈ 1, Yukawa coupling y_t ≈ 1
W⁺ boson propagation — massive gauge boson with width 2.085 GeV
W decay branching — leptonic (e⁺ν_e, μ⁺ν_μ, τ⁺ν_τ) vs hadronic (u d̄, c s̄)
leptonic W decay — clean signature, high purity for top mass measurement
hadronic W decay — larger branching ratio, combinatorial background
rejoin W decay products — combine leptonic and hadronic channels into W mass constraint
suppressed top decay arm — t → H⁺b (2HDM), t → cγ/Z/g (FCNC), BR < 10⁻³
rejoin all top decay channels — full decay width Γ_t = 1.33 GeV reconstructed
CPT-conjugate descent — antitop production and decay t̄ → W⁻b̄
compose top and antitop decay chains — tt̄ spin correlation preserved
tt̄ system identity — color-singlet/octet interference, spin entanglement
detector fixation — trigger accepts event, writes to permanent storage
electroweak vacuum boundary — process complete, gauge structure restored

phase_5.compiler_frontend: Standard Model Lagrangian → Feynman rules → helicity amplitudes → parton-level cross sections → Monte Carlo event generation (MadGraph, POWHEG) → detector simulation (Geant4)
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: gauge boson exchange: gluon (strong), W/Z (weak), photon (EM), Higgs (Yukawa); color flow via SU(3) strings
phase_5.memory_mechanism: quantum state in Fock space; parton distribution functions (PDFs) encode initial-state memory; top width Γ_t sets lifetime memory ~5×10⁻²⁵ s
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: perturbative ordering: LO → NLO → NNLO in α_s; factorization scale μ_F ~ m_t; renormalization scale μ_R ~ m_t; resummation for soft-gluon logs
phase_5.alfs_store: PDG top quark review; LHC combination (ATLAS+CMS) for mass, width, couplings; CKMfitter for V_tb

phase_6.cycle_cost: production: phase space suppression ~ (m_t/√s)² × α_s²; decay: width Γ_t = 1.33 GeV sets irreversible entropy production per top quark
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: initial state: two partons with PDF entropy S ~ ln(x₁x₂f₁f₂); low multiplicity, high virtuality
phase_6.post_cycle_state: final state: 6-10 partons/hadrons/leptons from tt̄ decay chain; high multiplicity, color reconnection, hadronization entropy
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS > 0 — weak decay is fundamentally irreversible (Γ_t ≠ 0); production requires energy input from beam; hadronization increases microstate count; cycle is entropy-generating, not conservative

grounding_reasoning:
⊣=𐑡: The top quark couples to all other quarks via the CKM matrix and to the Higgs field with maximal Yukawa coupling, forming a dense web of gauge and Yukawa interactions rather than a hierarchical, cyclic, enclosed, or holographic structure.
⊢=𐑼: The top quark is an elementary point-like particle with no internal spatial extent, operating as a local excitation in quantum fields.
⊞=𐑳: The top quark participates in fundamentally asymmetric interactions, coupling to the Higgs field with a unique Yukawa coupling of order unity while its weak isospin partner (bottom quark) couples far more weakly, and it decays almost exclusively to a W boson and bottom quark rather than engaging in symmetric exchange.
⊡=𐑷: The top quark's role as a massive fermion is not topologically protected; its mass and couplings are free parameters of the Standard Model that could be continuously deformed to zero or altered without crossing a topological boundary or violating a winding invariant.
⊙=𐑢: The top quark operates in a normal, subcritical regime without scale-free correlations or critical sensitivity; its large mass is a fixed parameter rather than a sign of proximity to a phase transition or critical point.
⊥=𐑖: The top quark exhibits persistent chirality through its fundamentally left-handed weak isospin doublet structure and right-handed singlet structure, which are structurally enforced by the electroweak gauge symmetry and cannot be interconverted without violating the Standard Model's chiral gauge structure.
≻=𐑑: The top quark undergoes irreversible structural transformation via weak decay (t → W⁺b) and participates in bond formation through strong and electroweak interactions that change its flavor, color, and momentum state.
≺=𐑿: The top quark carries a definite electric charge (+2/3) and weak isospin (+1/2), acting as a signed source for gauge fields without simultaneously serving as a sink or exhibiting self-complementary or mirror-symmetric polarity.
⋈=𐑐: The top quark's interactions are governed by precise gauge symmetries and a near-unity Yukawa coupling, resulting in deterministic, high-fidelity vertices in Feynman diagrams with branching ratios and cross-sections predicted to high precision by the Standard Model.
⊤=𐑧: The top quark's enormous mass (173 GeV) creates a high energy barrier for its production and suppresses flavor-changing processes, making its state kinetically frozen on typical QCD timescales and requiring high-energy external driving (e.g., TeV-scale collisions) to rearrange or produce it.
∈=𐑲: The top quark decays before it can hadronize, so its interactions remain confined to a single vertex with no propagation to neighboring particles or formation of extended correlations.
∋=𐑠: The top quark engages partners sequentially: it is produced in a hard scattering event, then decays via t → W⁺b, and the W subsequently decays, forming a strict temporal chain rather than a simultaneous or alternative partner set.
